players.product: Ultrastar DC SN861 PCIe Gen5 enterprise SSD

quarterly_data.signal: NBM demand visibility, CEO: a little more than 50% of FY2027 supply 'is already committed', and 'We already have POs for the year from those customers'; roughly 2/3 of FY2028 supply is committed. The NBMs include 'several of the largest hyperscalers in the world', which have given Sandisk 'forecasts years into the future that include quarter-by-quarter, month-by-month mix'; 'customers are giving us demand signals for all the way out to the end of the decade', and Sandisk continues 'to see very robust demand through the end of 2027, and into 2028'. Sandisk already has 'customers coming back for the second round of NBMs a quarter in', and Sandisk is 'definitely still in deep conversations with additional customers'. CFO: 'I think they are actually being conservative as they make commitments to us'; Sandisk will remain highly selective on additional NBMs, looking for strategic customers, a duration of around five years, growing volume requirements and attractive financials.
quarterly_data.figure: POs in hand for FY2027 NBM supply; customer demand signals to the end of the decade

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on margins and durability: 'I think mid-80s gross margin, I would characterize as a fair return'; the goal is to increase visibility and durability and 'get this kind of boom and bust out of it'. NBM supply is committed to customers willing to commit years in advance at the economics guided last quarter ('We guided to about 80% gross margin'), while 'The rest of the portfolio floats.' CEO: Sandisk now talks 'to the CFOs, the CEOs of the largest companies in the world', where this used to be a quarterly supply-chain and price negotiation. CFO: gross margin expanded 'every single quarter' over the last five quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: mid-80s gross margin = 'a fair return' (CEO); NBMs at about 80% gross margin

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on AI inference and NAND: 'We think, especially inference is a memory bound problem'; on KV cache, 'we just continue to get more optimistic on the requirements for NAND as AI gets more sophisticated, models get bigger, context lengths get longer, and then agentic is just a big multiplier on top of that'; the CEO is 'a very big believer now that the customers are driving the requirements in this market'. In High Bandwidth Flash, Sandisk continues 'to have deep engagements, both with cloud customers and device customers, about using that technology as an inference platform'; 'it's a little early to talk about pricing' on BiCS10 and HBF.

Supply and capex, CFO: capex dollars rise year over year because in node transitions 'you will first take the easiest or the cheapest transitions, then you would go on and do the more expensive ones', and in the prior year, with underutilized fabs, some tools could be reused; Sandisk remains committed to growing bits mid to high teens. CEO: in FY2026 Sandisk 'secured our manufacturing and supply base through the next decade'; 'We can grow in excess of the market rates we're talking about just through nodal transitions.'

CEO on edge markets: PCs and smartphones 'are working through a period of adjustment' as demand shifts toward AI-enabled devices and premium configurations, driving higher storage content, particularly in smartphones; in PCs, 'OEMs are growing revenue and expanding margin on a more profitable mix'. 'We expect these markets to return to growth in calendar year 2027', and 'we expect increases in content per device through future refresh cycles'; emerging physical-AI edge uses include automotive, robotics and on-device agentic AI.
